scope.inria: All 420 records in the files selected by the original driver's file/1 facts. Inactive auxiliary/experimental files, including the documented non-runnable halt file, are not added to that inventory.
scope.examples: All 567 calls to test_true/1, test_false/1, test_val/3 and error_test/2 in sec*.pl. IDs identify file, top-level term ordinal and check ordinal; line identifies the containing clause. Prose/manual output expectations are not counted as additional assertions.

inria: Retain the original result/substitution machinery and expected records. Supply append/3, member/2 and length/2 as private ordinary Prolog clauses; the distribution assumes these helpers but does not define them.

Replace the two harness-only UNIV error-recognition guards with formal-error-name recognition, and prepend formal-error comparison before list-of-substitution comparison. Native cons applications do not have ISO list-cell functors. Calls under test are unchanged.

Replay all previous goals in the same input file before the target and read each record at execution time. This retains double_quotes and database effects inside each isolated worker. Predecessor comparisons are not rerun: they have no intended external effects.
Record the runtime-read target as executed_goal; inventory goal text was parsed using the initial flags and can differ for later double-quoted records.
examples: Load utilities, database and each section through native term forms. Resolve include/ensure_loaded relative to fixtures with optional .pl extension; queue initialization until loading completes.
Alpha-rename the sec74.pl private AND/2 helper and its operator spelling to HODGSON_AND/2 to avoid sprolog's protected AND/2 alias. Add GO7_4 -> GO_74 to repair the upstream initialization spelling.

Instrument each assertion call with an ID and stop after its result. Preserve copying, first-solution and unifying test_val expectations, and formal exception matching. Report exceptions in test_false as failures; the original logger could let an exception appear successful.

Run the containing zero-arity predicate for each target; sec89.pl uses test_89 to preserve database-update order. Verification helpers omitted by that entry point receive their corresponding asserta/assertz setup explicitly.
Route LOG/1 and LOG_NL/0 away from the tested stream; manual prose/output assertions are not automatically checked. Success/failure/exception checks in those goals still run.
Run test_halt1 in a separate process; require the target-start marker and actual exit status 7.

applicability.inria/abolish:4: Requires finite max_arity; skip when max_arity=unbounded.
applicability.inria/functor:17: Requires finite max_arity; skip when max_arity=unbounded.
applicability.inria/atom_codes:11: Assumes character code 1000 is unsupported; skip when char_code/2 accepts it.
applicability.inria/number_codes:14: Assumes character code 1000 is unsupported; skip when char_code/2 accepts it.
applicability.examples/sec816.pl:17:3: Assumes character code 9999 is unsupported; skip when char_code/2 accepts it.

known_upstream_limitations: These are 1999 distributions, not an updated executable specification of all corrigenda.
Several floating-point expected values are rounded or require exact historical representations; no tolerance is silently introduced.
Some error classes/culprits and substitution expectations differ from current interpretations. Non-model discrepancies remain FAIL pending review.

Examples contain historical code/expectation mistakes, such as set_ionput in write_read_term2, a section-7.4 lookup of d7_4 against dis7_4 values, and a manually specified sub_atom result table. They are not silently rewritten.

sec78.pl:9:8 expects type_error(callable,1) for call((write(3),1)), while INRIA call:10 expects the whole conjunction for the same goal. Whole-body conversion now preserves the ISO culprit; the contradictory example remains FAIL.
